front.title: Water and
front.note: Two short films by a photographer: light on moving water, and machines turning, each filmed as pure form.

pages.title: H2O
pages.synopsis: A study of light on water. It begins with streams over stones and, as the camera grows absorbed in texture and design, ends close to an abstract film: reflections that are only light, shadow and line.
credits: Photographed and edited by Ralph Steiner

pages.title: Mechanical
pages.synopsis: Gears, cams, screws and linkages, filmed close and turning, without a word. Machines looked at as forms in motion, each shot composed like a still life.
credits: Photographed and edited by Ralph Steiner

pages.title: About
paras: Ralph Steiner (1899 – 1986) was an American photographer who began making films at the end of the 1920s. His first, H2O, looked at water until it became pattern; it was much admired by the avant-garde audiences of its day.
This is a sample site built from two of his films, H2O and Mechanical Principles, both in the public domain. The words here are the sample's own.

pages.title: Contact
paras: A sample site. The films are by Ralph Steiner and are in the public domain; the copies used here are on Wikimedia Commons.
Latent Wall shows them to show what a filmmaker's site can be.
